source_evidence: Medial compartment cartilage: Broad-based area of grade 4 chondrosis along the central the anterior weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle extending over 1.0 cm mediolateral dimension, and up to 1.9 cm anterior posterior dimension.
context_quotes: Medial compartment cartilage: Broad-based area of grade 4 chondrosis along the central the anterior weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle extending over 1.0 cm mediolateral dimension, and up to 1.9 cm anterior posterior dimension.
Diffuse thinning of the cartilage of the medial tibial plateau with areas of up to grade 3 chondrosis medially.
Moderate to advanced medial compartment osteoarthritis with areas of to grade 4 chondrosis in the medial femoral condyle.

Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Scattered areas of up to grade 2/3 chondrosis at the medial patellar facet measuring up to 0.5 cm mediolateral dimension. Grade 2/3 chondrosis in the medial trochlea.
reasoning: The new primary literature changes the strength of any universal numeric assertion: grade4 does not always mean the same depth across MRI systems. I explicitly accept root’s limited counterexample and do not claim universal numbering.

The exact report, however, gives a measured cartilage lesion, calls it grade4 chondrosis, separately describes grade3 areas within medial tibial thinning, and calls the medial OA moderate to advanced. The comparative grade2/3 patellofemoral description is lower in the same report. I find an Outerbridge-like depth interpretation more persuasive in this narrative context; this is a contextual clinical-language inference, not proof of the reporting convention or a measured probability.

The 2015 primary MRI study directly defines gradeIV as full-thickness loss. That supports the concrete interpretation already made in both of my source freezes. The Meredith study confirms an alternative research score, but neither source establishes that our report used its specific scale. Research-score nonuniversality alone does not persuade me that this measured grade4 chondrosis is an established positive-label error.

The source itself never names the grading system or independently states a literal depth fraction. Root’s more conservative uncertainty therefore remains a defensible competing extraction interpretation. I cannot certify the reporting framework, and I do not turn the ordinary-language inference into a new global mapping rule.

I retain my positive source interpretation and decline additional acceptance at this stage. Keep the item unresolved, outside the12 accepted changes, and in the pending cartilage QA scope. Resolving the project’s admissible grading interpretation or obtaining source-convention evidence would be a separate adjudication; do not decide through application order or silently amend the frozen protocol.
